I need to clarify what "Secreted to blood" resolves to in this data model. Let me test combined filters and check a known pancreas-enriched secreted gene:

No matching proteins — the count is **0**.

**How I determined this (all from tool results):**

1. Filtering the Human Protein Atlas with protein class = **"Secreted to blood"** returns exactly 6 genes: **IL10, CD40, EFNA1, SEMA3E, SEMA3C, LNPEP** (confirmed with maxResults = 10000, so the full class).

2. Combined filter (protein class = Secreted to blood AND tissue-specific = pancreas) returns an **empty set**.

3. I manually verified each of the 6 genes with `get_tissue_expression` — none is RNA "Tissue enriched" for pancreas:

| Gene | RNA tissue specificity | Liver nTPM | Pancreas nTPM |
|------|------------------------|-----------|---------------|
| IL10 | Tissue enhanced | 1.0 | 0.2 |
| CD40 | Tissue enhanced | 14.7 | 15.6 |
| EFNA1 | Tissue enhanced | 476.5 | 58.0 |
| SEMA3E | Low tissue specificity | 0.1 | 0.3 |
| SEMA3C | Low tissue specificity | 1.2 | 2.5 |
| LNPEP | Low tissue specificity | 4.0 | 4.8 |

Since none of the six "Secreted to blood" genes has RNA-level tissue enrichment in pancreas (and five of the six are detected in liver), **the intersection with "tissue enriched in pancreas at RNA level but not detected in liver" contains 0 genes — there are no gene symbols to list.**
